title: Harden a sloppy 4-service stack through a sealed 6-scenario ops campaign
goal: The stack in assets/gc-383/stack/ runs, barely, with the operational posture of a weekend prototype: floating image tags, no healthchecks, no persistence, no restart policies, and a broken HTTP surface. The sealed campaign harness scores six scenarios: image pinning, four working healthchecks, an HTTP contract with a /health endpoint, cache data surviving a service restart, database and cache state surviving a full down/up cycle (which forces named volumes and real persistence config), and a worker that self-heals after being killed. These interact - a healthcheck that probes the wrong thing blocks the persistence scenarios because the harness waits on healthy states - so you must plan the hardening order, drill each scenario yourself, and re-run the sealed harness to catch regressions your fixes introduce. Only files under assets/gc-383/stack/ may be edited.
process_expectations: A campaign plan artifact orders the six scenarios by dependency and names the compose/config mechanism for each, before any edit
Each scenario is drilled in isolation with self-run commands (restart drills, down/up drills, kill drills) and raw outputs are captured
Scenario failures are tracked by identity (e.g. 'S4 red: AOF disabled so restart wipes keys', 'S2 red: worker healthcheck probes wrong host'), with the fix that cleared each
Cross-scenario regressions are explicitly checked: after each fix, previously green scenarios are re-verified and any regression is logged, not papered over
The scenarios_passed trajectory across full harness runs is reported honestly, including runs where a fix reduced the score
